metric.concurrency.normalization_rationale: Below midpoint due to lack of true CPU-bound thread parallelism and no compile-time race safety; credited for solid native async model and primitives.
observations: GIL prevents true multi-threaded CPU parallelism in CPython.
multiprocessing gives real parallelism but with serialization overhead.
asyncio provides native async/await cooperative concurrency, well designed for I/O-bound work.
Rich stdlib concurrency primitives (Lock, Queue, concurrent.futures) comparable to Java util.concurrent.
Structured concurrency (asyncio.TaskGroup, 3.11+) is a genuine recent improvement.
Free-threaded/no-GIL mode (PEP 703) exists but not yet default/mature.

metric.ffi_interoperability_design.normalization_rationale: Above midpoint for strong native in-language FFI mechanisms; below top tier due to marshaling overhead, ABI instability, and GIL friction.
observations: CPython C-API is a first-class in-language FFI mechanism.
ctypes in stdlib allows calling shared libraries without writing C glue.
Buffer protocol (PEP 3118) enables zero-copy interop with native code.
Boxed PyObject model requires marshaling overhead vs native-ABI languages (Rust/Zig/C++).
Historically unstable binary ABI across CPython minor versions.
GIL requires explicit acquire/release around native calls for concurrency.
